articles.title: 700,000 still without power after Thanksgiving storms batter both coasts
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people were left without power after storms hit the East and West coasts, prompting road closures and flight delays on Thanksgiving. Around 700,000 homes remain without power as of 3 a.m. ET Friday, on the East coast and in areas of Missouri. Weather warnings are in place along the East and West coasts for gales and hazardous seas, respectively, while a handful of states in the Northeast and Northwest of the country are under winter weather advisories. Thanksgiving saw thousands of flight delays and hundreds of cancellations, as well as road flooding in coastal areas and heavy snowfall in areas of Illinois and Missouri. There were more than 2,500 flight delays and 462 cancellations within, into or out of the U.S., according to FlightAware . This follows more than 7,000 delays Wednesday as travelers attempted to make their way across the country to celebrate Thanksgiving. The storm flooded coastal areas along the Eastern Seaboard from North Carolina through New Jersey, with highways and roads shut down due to floodwaters and high winds. More than 830,000 homes and businesses were without power yesterday, led by Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia, according to PowerOutage.us , with more than 100,000 having power restored by early Friday. About 42 million people were under high wind warnings or wind advisories as of 4:50 a.m. ET, and around 64 million are under coastal flood warnings or advisories, according to the National Weather Service . In New York City, a state of emergency was declared by Gov. Kathy Hochul and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed until Saturda y. California battled surging king tides with an entire section of the Pacifica Pier demolished by waves. articles.title: Macy's parade faced a historic postponement. Saturday's forecast is looking better.
articles.summary: The annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is set to go ahead Saturday after being postponed for the first time in its history due to severe weather . The 100th parade will now step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 28. NBC and Peacock will air it at 8:30 a.m. in the Eastern, Central and Mountain time zones and at 7:30 a.m. Pacific, according to NBC , with a Spanish-language simulcast on Telemundo. Some performers have needed to scramble to ensure they can take part in the rescheduled event. The Pride of Pearland Marching Band at Pearland High School in Texas raised $350,000 after launching a fundraiser to ensure they could extend their stay in the city. “I am still shocked at it, to be honest with you,” said Ryan Demkovich, the band's director. The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign's marching band will also perform after launching a fundraiser to cover the additional $175,000 costs. "We are doing this parade on Saturday," band director Barry Houser told cheering members of Marching Illini, in a video posted to the group's Instagram account . Other performers still scheduled to appear on the NBC Insider site include RAYE, Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Mckenna Grace, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots and Queen Latifah. At least one act will miss the new date, however. The University of Alabama said its Million Dollar Band will head home to play at a football game, the Associated Press reported . The casts of "Wicked," "Hamilton" and "The Rocky Horror Show" are also slated to perform Saturday. The decision to postpone the parade was made ahead of a storm that brought heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding to the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day. Concerns about whether balloons would be allowed to fly safely mounted as the National Weather Service issued a high-wind warning of potentially "strong and damaging wind gusts.” "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said in a statement. The weather forecast for Saturday looks significantly better than the high winds experienced by New Yorkers Thursday. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani acknowledged the "inconvenience" of the rescheduling, but said the move was necessary to protect the safety of participants and spectators.  "On Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe," he said. Macy's executive producer Will Coss was unable to confirm whether all acts scheduled to perform on Thanksgiving will still be able to participate on Saturday, but said he was "optimistic" that organizers will be able to "maintain the parade that we set out to produce." The decision marks the first time the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, although it has previously been modified due to weather disruptions. In 1971, all balloons were grounded ahead of the parade because of gusty winds and heavy rainfall. The city also established regulations in 1998 requiring large balloons to be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph after an incident during the 1997 parade, in which a Cat in the Hat balloon critically injured a woman after it struck a lamppost. articles.title: EPA detects no airborne lead after Iowa blast but is still testing soil and water
articles.summary: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) issued an "all clear" notice around a U.S. Army facility in Iowa after the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, was blown up in a controlled detonation Wednesday. The blast, which took place at 10 a.m. ET at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, went ahead after a federal appeals court cleared the way for the detonation amid concerns over the environmental impact of a potential toxic lead dust plume. "FEMA has issued an All Clear around Iowa Army Ammunition Plant," the U.S. Army said in a social media post Wednesday night , adding that there was "zero" airborne lead detected. The Environmental Protection Agency said Thursday that its real-time air monitors had detected no airborne lead anywhere in the region since the blast. Crews have collected more than 1,000 air, water, soil and dust samples since the detonation, on top of 1,591 taken beforehand, and the first lab results could arrive as early as Friday, the agency said in an update . On Thursday, EPA crews were sampling schools, playgrounds, day cares and churches in the area and running a second round of drinking water tests, the agency said. Lee Zeldin, the head of the Environmental Protection Agency, said that while sensors near the blast site were showing no signs of lead, parents should still take precautions when they go outside. "Residents are encouraged to wipe down outdoor surfaces that children touch … such as play sets, railings and window sills with a wet cloth," he said. The blast, which transforms the explosive lead azide into elemental lead, was first scheduled for Nov. 20, but was postponed amid a court fight and public concern. On Monday, a federal appeals court cleared the way for the detonation to go ahead after environmental groups sued to stop it. Scientists had also warned that much about the environmental impact was unknown. The Army said detonating the stockpile as soon as possible was the safest option because it was degrading and might explode uncontrollably at any time as the weather cooled. Officials worked to limit the impact of the detonation, with earthen barriers erected and foam and water poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons of lead azide to absorb much of the blast. The EPA said it had granted an emergency permit to detonate the stockpile because a "controlled detonation during optimal weather conditions and incorporating robust mitigation measures, compared to an uncontrolled explosion, significantly reduces the potential reach and concentration of lead dust landing on surfaces, such as homes and windows." articles.title: Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up at China site tied to alleged spy Alice Huang
articles.summary: (Bloomberg) -- A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. Most Read from Bloomberg SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Roles in AI Restructure Trump Calls GDP Numbers ‘Fake,’ Demands Probe After Revision South Africa Sentences Russia Army Recruit as Ukraine Urges Action Nvidia Rehires Huang in Stunning Reversal After Trump Push Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After Chip Curbs The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. A second firm Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server — which also relies on Blackwell chips — at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data center that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia’s most powerful data center products, and they’ve always been illegal to ship to China without a US license. President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn’t want these chips — which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models — going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-meter-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge. Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company’s products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars. It’s unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site — described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan’s Gigabyte Technology Co., which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company. This sort of gear often passes through several hands — including local distribution networks — before it’s installed in data centers. In many cases, products that were ultimately smuggled into China were originally sold to parties in unrestricted areas. Bloomberg provided the rack’s serial number to Gigabyte, seeking information about to whom Gigabyte had originally sold the hardware and when. It declined to answer those questions, citing company policy. The firm “conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations,” a spokesperson said in an emailed statement. “All transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time.” Shanghai Shuoyao — the company that procured the GB300 rack and offered it as collateral — is active at the data center linked to Alice Huang and also has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg has reported. Shanghai Shuoyao, which hasn’t responded to Bloomberg queries over the past year, confirmed this month in a rare public statement that it is one of Megaspeed’s service providers, describing the partnership as “limited to ordinary commercial cooperation.” Megaspeed, meanwhile, used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024 to describe its largest data center to investors, dubbing the site a “specific area” facility in an unnamed country. Bloomberg does not have evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware there, and Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in response to the US probe. The company has not answered repeated queries about the Yangtze River Delta Project. Nor has Nvidia, which for years insisted that there was no black market for its products and didn’t respond to questions for this story. The Trump administration this month put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, citing a significant risk of involvement in chip diversion. Alice Huang in 2023 founded Megaspeed, a so-called neocloud that won a coveted stamp of approval from Nvidia within four days of its creation, and went on to become the chipmaker’s largest Southeast Asian customer. She also has ties to a number of companies that invested in the Yangtze River Delta Project, which counts Kang Wei as its president. Kang has been introduced at times as Alice Huang’s romantic partner, people familiar with the matter said. It’s unclear how far along operators are in meeting their overall goal for that project, which at 800,000 servers would be on par with hyperscale facilities used by companies like OpenAI. It’s also unclear what mix of servers they plan to use. The parameters they’ve outlined in construction plans reviewed by Bloomberg — specifically, the total processing power as compared to the energy input — would be extremely difficult to satisfy with chips from Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co. Still, the smuggled hardware disclosed in the filings reviewed by Bloomberg is just a fraction of what they’d need. These documents only cover hardware offered as collateral for loans — providing a small snapshot of the operators’ ambitions, while also underscoring how some Chinese financial institutions, including with government ties, were aware that restricted hardware was getting into China and willing to lend capital on those assets. Bloomberg was unable to reach the leasing company that lent money to Shanghai Kezhan, nor Shanghai Innovation Bank, which in addition to the money it lent Shanghai Shuoyao, also provided a 200 million yuan loan to another company called Shanghai Longjie, similarly with restricted Nvidia chips as collateral. Shanghai Longjie — which has the same parent company as Shanghai Shuoyao — disclosed in documents filed to regulators that it has servers containing Nvidia’s earlier Hopper-generation chips, which are illegal to ship to China without Washington’s permission, Bloomberg reported this month. That hardware was manufactured by Super Micro Computer Inc. and Dell Technologies Inc. It’s unclear whether the shipments had US approval. Those aren’t the only Hopper chips at the Yangtze River Delta Project. Shanghai Kezhan, the company that described the GB200 server in filings last year, also disclosed that it has 32 servers with H200 chips there. These products had a Gigabyte prefix in their model name, but the documents didn’t include serial numbers — making them harder to trace. Shanghai Kezhan is headquartered about half a kilometer from the Yangtze River Delta Project, at the same commercial complex where Shanghai Shuoyao solicited engineers to work on Nvidia H100 and H200 chips — two restricted models. In February 2024, both of these firms added “imports and exports” to their business activities, according to data from Qizhidao, a company information provider. The same month, Megaspeed’s original parent — the Chinese gaming giant 7Road — obtained 16.7% of Shanghai Kezhan via a subsidiary the gaming company bought from Alice Huang in 2019. The other 83.3% of Kezhan is ultimately owned by NeXPower Japan, according to Qizhidao. Japan’s official companies registry returned only one company named NeXPower, which was established in March 2025. Caixin, a Chinese business news outlet, said the Tokyo firm is controlled by Alice Huang. Bloomberg has been unable to reach NeXPower for comment. Chinese-speaking staffers at the firm’s registered address wouldn’t confirm that was NeXPower’s office, and shut the door after Bloomberg News asked about their relationship with Alice Huang and Shanghai Kezhan. On the intercom was a message saying they are working and will not respond to media questions. The registered address of the company’s director appeared to be a vacated residence. In May 2025, records compiled by Big Trade Data show, Shanghai Kezhan received a shipment worth $11 million, flown from Malaysia to Shanghai Pudong International Airport with the company as consignee. The customs document described the shipment as “storage chassis,” referring to a structure that houses components of a storage server. But the product code it was assigned to was 847150, which denotes computing servers. The shipment’s unit price was $264,108, too costly for a storage chassis — but within the price range of servers powered by Nvidia’s Hopper chips. --With assistance from Mari Kiyohara, Natsuko Katsuki and Mayumi Negishi. articles.title: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico
articles.summary: Mexico's president has blasted the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration after it set up anonymous tip lines in the country, accusing American officials of "interference" and not doing enough to fight fentanyl and corruption inside their own borders. President Claudia Sheinbaum, in harsh comments Thursday, read excerpts from a new investigation by The Associated Press revealing how the DEA allowed at least 1.4 million counterfeit fentanyl pills to go unseized as it spent eight months tracking a drug trafficking ring flooding the Southwest with deadly drugs. "The DEA has plenty of work to do in its own country. A lot," Sheinbaum said, pointing to the AP report. "The first thing it should do is investigate corruption in the United States linked to organized crime, or what they call terrorist groups." "It's clearly an act of interference," Sheinbaum added. Imagine, she mused, if Mexico "opened a WhatsApp service for reporting corruption in the United States. How would the U.S. government view that?" Sheinbaum's angry response comes less than 24 hours after DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced the tip lines on his X account, encouraging Mexicans to denounce members of criminal networks in Sinaloa state, the corrupt officials who support them and people who launder money to finance narcoterrorism. "Your information matters. Your identity and your safety matter," Cole said, specifying that tips submitted via Signal, WhatsApp and email would be handled confidentially. U.S. steps up pressure on Mexico The United States has stepped up pressure on Mexico to fight the cartels and has even offered to deploy troops on Mexican soil, something Sheinbaum has ruled out while maintaining that there will be security cooperation with Washington, "but without subordination." On Nov. 20, Mexican military forces captured drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, alias "El Chapo Isidro," a key ally of a Sinaloa cartel faction. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives , while the U.S. State Department offered a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest. The military operation o capture him tsparked panic in the region, sending civilians fleeing from erupting gunfire. Elsewhere in the state, suspected gang members reportedly erected improvised roadblocks. In clashes with security forces , 16 cartel suspects were killed, officials said, and four soldiers also died. Mexico requested Washington's support for the operation, and the United States sent a drone to help gather information about the drug lord's whereabouts. The U.S. has requested Meza Flores' extradition, but Mexican Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said he will be tried in Mexico. Chapo Isidro's capture came just days after Sheinbaum met President Trump on the sidelines of a summit in Asia. Mr. Trump, who has pushed Mexico to do more to tackle drug gangs, said Friday that the two had discussed trade and security. The Mexican government has knocked out several cartel kingpins. Chief among them was Mexico's most powerful cartel leader , known as "El Mencho ," who was killed in February. Similar to the capture of Meza Flores, the dramatic operation resulted in a burst of violence and burning cars. Although cooperation between the two countries went smoothly in that operation, tensions arose between Mexico and Washington in late April after federal prosecutors in New York made public a drug trafficking indictment against Sinaloa Gov. Rubén Rocha Moya , a member of Mexico's governing party. He and nine other officials were accused of collaborating with a faction of the Sinaloa cartel, which the Trump administration has designated a foreign terrorist organization. Amid the controversy, Rocha Moya took an indefinite leave of absence, and his bank accounts in Mexico were frozen. But Mexican authorities refused to carry out the U.S. request to arrest him. Former Sinaloa Security Secretary Gerardo Mérida Sánchez surrendered to U.S. authorities in May. DEA accused of "walking" fentanyl DEA whistleblowers in June revealed to the AP how agents in New Mexico in recent years permitted hundreds of thousands of fentanyl pills to go unseized. At the time, the DEA denied it ever knowingly allowed the trafficking of a synthetic opioid the White House has designated a "weapon of mass destruction." That denial, however, was further contradicted by new AP findings that the DEA permitted at least 1.4 million additional pills to be trafficked between August 2024 and April 2025 as it closed in on the largest fentanyl bust in U.S. history. The AP based its tally on thousands of pages of court documents, investigative records, detailed wiretap reports and 12 hours of DEA surveillance footage showing dealers moving large packages of pills in plastic bins and duffel bags that passed through highly transited hotels, apartment complexes, Airbnb rentals and self-storage facilities in six states. The Mexican president in her comments Thursday called the DEA's decision to permit fentanyl to hit the streets the "Fast and Furious of Fentanyl," a reference to the 2011 gun-walking scandal in which straw buyers smuggled some 2,000 assault weapons into Mexico with the intent of tracing the firearms to cartel leaders. "What is the United States doing in the United States?" Sheinbaum asked. "We have a prosecutor's office here, and the Security Ministry works here. So they should pay close attention to the other side of the border." The DEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Cole said a channel for submitting tips about the state of Jalisco would be made public Thursday. The state is a stronghold of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel, known by its Spanish initials CJNG, which Washington also designated a terrorist organization. Meanwhile, a veteran DEA agent also told CBS News last month the agency has contributed to the problem by allowing fentanyl pills to reach the streets. "For three years, I've told my DEA managers that we're allowing dangerous amounts of fentanyl to hit the street, and we're doing nothing to stop it, and they didn't listen to me," DEA Special Agent David Howell told CBS News in his first television interview. articles.title: Hackers breach U.S. Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform
articles.summary: By Mike Stone and Raphael Satter WASHINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion ‌at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that ‌the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen. In a statement ​to Reuters, the Air Force said it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities." A ONE-STOP SHOP Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force's IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance. Among ‌them are the Air Force's Cloud-Based Command and Control, which ⁠collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 US Air Force locations around the world. SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One ⁠until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. Cloud One is among the US military's biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources. "A breach here is a big deal," one of the sources said. Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, to assess the ​damage, ​one of the sources said. Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment. A RANGE OF ​DISRUPTION The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. ‌Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused. Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked. All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity. One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders ‌in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the ​movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case. Reuters ​could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers. STRING OF HACKS News ​of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability ‌of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas. The ​US government already has been dealing with ​the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department. Cloud One has long ​been in the crosshairs of hackers. In a 2023 commentary carried ‌by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One's leadership touted what they called a "100% success rate" in beating back what they said was a "staggering" ​number of attempts to penetrate the platform. "There is no room for error when it comes to security," Cloud One's leadership wrote. (Reporting by ​Mike Stone and Raphael Satter in Washington; Editing by Chris Sanders and Will Dunham) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/exclusive-hackers-breach-us-air-110252874.html

articles.title: Supreme Court to tackle AR-15 bans in blockbuster 2nd Amendment case
articles.summary: A gun store employee holds an AR-15 semi-automatic rifle in Salem, Oregon, on March 6, 2025. - Kevin Neri/Statesman Journal/USA Today Network/Reuters Fourteen years after a lone gunman carried out the deadliest elementary school shooting in American history, the Supreme Court is turning to a bitter legal fight over whether communities may outlaw the type of weapon used in that massacre — a popular class of semi-automatic guns that includes the AR-15. In one of the most notable Second Amendment cases to reach the 6-3 conservative court in decades, the justices will hear arguments Wednesday over state and local bans on “assault-style” weapons, such as the AR-15, some of which were enacted or strengthened in response to a dramatic increase in mass shootings since 20 first graders and six educators were killed in 2012 at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut. For the government officials and gun safety groups defending the bans, the memory of deadly shootings involving the AR-15 is a driving force. “The basic function of government is to keep its citizenry safe, and these guns are so incredibly dangerous in a densely populated area like Chicago,” said Cook County State’s Attorney Eileen O’Neill Burke, a Democrat, who is defending one of the bans at the Supreme Court. “One hundred percent of the children who were hit with this weapon at Sandy Hook died.” But two trends have emerged in recent years that benefit gun rights groups. First, far more Americans own an AR-15 today — as many as 26 million people, according to one estimate — than even a decade ago. The Supreme Court acknowledged as much last year, noting in a unanimous opinion that the weapons are “widely legal,” purchased by “many ordinary consumers” and that the AR–15 “is the most popular rifle in the country.” Second, the court’s conservatives has quickly and vastly expanded the scope and meaning of the Second Amendment. In a series of landmark decisions, the court found for the first time that the Constitution provides individual Americans a right to own a handgun at home and to carry that weapon outside . It has made it easier to bring guns onto private property open to the public, such as stores. It has required governments defending gun laws to find a “historical antecedent,” a similar rule on the books when the Second Amendment was ratified in 1791. In a 2008 decision that gun rights groups will cite heavily during arguments this week, the late conservative Justice Antonin Scalia suggested that the Second Amendment protects weapons that are in “common use.” The plaintiffs challenging the AR-15 bans in Connecticut and Cook County, Illinois, use the phrase “common use” 56 times in their main brief supporting their position. Twenty-seven wooden angel figures stand in a wooded area beside a road, in Newtown, Connecticut, on December 16, 2012, following the mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School. - Lisa Wiltse/Corbis/Getty Images The Trump administration, which is backing the gun rights groups, used that phrase 49 times in its own brief filed in September. Kostas Moros, director of legal research and education at the Second Amendment Foundation, acknowledged that AR-15s are dangerous. But he noted that all firearms are dangerous — and, despite that, the framers protected Americans’ ability to own them in the Constitution. “They gave the people the uninfringeable right to keep and bear arms, and that is a right of the people — not of the states, not of the government — to decide,” Moros said. Dangerous and unusual Blockbuster appeals at the Supreme Court are often complicated. The case over AR-15 bans, by contrast, is relatively straightforward. Connecticut and Cook County are leaning into the Supreme Court’s reasoning in a 2022 precedent, New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen , which struck down a strict requirement in New York that residents show cause to obtain a carry permit. As part of that decision, a 6-3 majority concluded that in order to survive a Second Amendment challenge, modern-day gun regulations needed to have some grounding in the “nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation.” While the court has tinkered with that standard in subsequent decisions, the state and county say there is an extensive history — dating to medieval times — of English laws banning especially dangerous weapons. Their briefs spend considerable ink discussing bans on crossbows and certain lances. “From fourteenth-century England to twenty-first century America, governments have restricted weapons because of their unusually dangerous properties,” Connecticut officials told the Supreme Court this fall. “In each instance, legislatures have determined that a weapon is atypically lethal relative to its peers — and so have acted to prevent that weapon’s use.” Thomas, who wrote the majority opinion in Bruen, seemed to dismiss the relevance of some of that same history when it came to handguns, noting that one of those laws came “more than 200 years before the birth of Shakespeare, more than 350 years before the Salem Witch Trials.” But he flicked at the idea that banning “launcegays” may have made sense given that they were carried when “one intended to engage in lawful combat.” Supporters of the ban see that logic as a potential opening. Connecticut and Cook County — which includes Chicago — note the AR-15’s ties to its military counterpart, the M16. They note that AR-15s, like other long guns, are more accurate than handguns. The weapons, which first came onto the commercial market in the 1960s, can feature a bullet that tumbles on its axis when it hits a target, creating more significant wounds, the state and county said. The weapon’s design limits recoil more than many hunting rifles, allowing a shooter to maintain control even during rapid, semi-automatic firing. Burke, the Cook County prosecutor, said the weapon’s range and design make it “unbelievably dangerous for law enforcement.” “It was designed for the military,” she said. “It was designed to take out enemy combatants at the greatest distance possible.” A bullet impact crater is seen in concrete, after a gunman opened fire with an AR-15 at the Edmund Burke School in Washington, DC, on on April 28, 2022. - Ricky Carioti/The Washington Post/Getty Images Gun rights groups focus first on the weapon’s popularity. Only 11 states have approved bans on AR-15s, and so the rifles are widely available and in use by gun owners across the country, the vast majority of whom never commit a crime. The plaintiffs challenging the bans described the AR-15 as the “paradigmatic American rifle” in written arguments. According to one survey, roughly 30% of American gun owners have an AR-15 or similar rifle, which works out to 26 million people. A Washington Post-Ipsos survey from 2022 works out to about 16 million Americans. Those numbers alone, the plaintiffs said, should resolve the case in their favor. Scalia’s 2008 precedent in District of Columbia v. Heller “stands for the proposition that arms in common use cannot be banned,” the plaintiffs told the justices. The challengers also reject the idea that an AR-15 is more dangerous than other guns. They argue that the caliber most often used is smaller than that of many traditional hunting rifles. And they scoff at some of the warnings from government officials as bordering on science fiction. “These are ordinary rifles,” the plaintiffs told the justices in one brief, “not phasers from Star Trek.” “If a madman was going to my daughter’s school, I wouldn’t feel much better if he quote-unquote only had a Glock, versus an AR-15,” said Moros, whose group is one of the plaintiffs challenging the bans. “My theory has always been, you need to make targets less vulnerable to attack, rather than worry so much about what the particular gun does.” Counting to five Connecticut and Cook County face headwinds for another reason: At least four conservative justices have signaled skepticism with the bans to varying degrees. If that holds, it means the government will need to find at least two justices to reach a five-vote majority, assuming the court’s three-justice liberal wing supports them. Justice Clarence Thomas, among the court’s most stalwart conservatives, made clear in 2015 that he felt lower courts upholding the bans were “relegating the Second Amendment to a second-class right.” A year later, in a case involving stun guns, Justice Samuel Alito wrote that “the relative dangerousness of a weapon is irrelevant when the weapon belongs to a class of arms commonly used for lawful purposes.” Justice Neil Gorsuch has been less clear, though he voted last year to hear a similar case dealing with Maryland’s AR-15 ban. Associate Supreme Court Justices Samuel Alito, Jr., Clarence Thomas and Brett Kavanaugh attend President Donald Trump's second inauguration, in the Rotunda of the US Capitol on January 20, 2025. - Chip Somodevilla/Pool/AFP/Getty Images Justice Brett Kavanaugh, a conservative who is closer to the center than Alito or Thomas, wrote in the Maryland case that the state was “something of an outlier” by having a ban on the weapons. And, he said, given that millions of Americans own one, the challengers had a “strong argument” that AR-15s are protected by the Second Amendment. As an appeals court judge in 2011, Kavanaugh also dissented from a decision upholding a Washington, DC, ban on “assault-style” rifles. If that holds, it means there will be an enormous amount of focus on Chief Justice John Roberts and Justice Amy Coney Barrett at the arguments Wednesday. Still, groups that support additional gun regulations say they’re optimistic about the appeal. The earlier cases dealt with handguns, they note, which are more commonly used for home defense. And most federal appeals courts to review the laws — including the 7th Circuit in the Cook County case and the 2nd Circuit in the Connecticut dispute — upheld the laws. “The chief and Justice Barrett have articulated a history-based test that looks for something useful in the history. It doesn’t just look for a Constitution frozen in time. It looks for a way in which the Constitution can still have relevance,” said Billy Clark, associate litigation director at the Giffords Law Center. The chief justice, Clark said, is “someone who recognizes the consequences” of the court’s decisions, and “I think is going to be cautious about saying that these sorts of weapons are constitutionally enshrined.” For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/27/politics/supreme-court-ar-15-ban-second-amendment

articles.title: Zelensky criticizes 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship
articles.summary: Watch: Zelensky questions "strange" Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, criticising Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" and saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles were costing Ukrainian lives. In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president complained the US was not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks, and called it "strange" that Trump posted a photo of himself embracing Putin. "Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English. "He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two. Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States. Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv. The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it. He said talks were expected to resume in December. On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility". But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything. And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced . The Kremlin appears to be resisting. Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend Ukraine urgently needs the talks to move forward and bring five exhausting years of Russia's full-scale invasion to an end. Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high. So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect". "When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right," he said. The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold. Questioned again on Thursday about calling Putin a friend, Trump told reporters: "We want to stop killing. I could say he's not a friend... I want to make a deal." He added: "I could walk in and say, I don't like you, and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelensky and Putin. "You know... the biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other." [BBC] In the meantime, Kyiv is struggling to defend its skies. The air alerts, day and night, are now a draining feature of everyday life. As Russian ballistic missiles target power stations and bridges, jet-powered drones are launched daily at central Kyiv and other big cities. Ukraine launches hundreds of drones at targets in Russia in response. Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving. But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Americans were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems. "It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more… It's a pity. We have huge questions with this," Zelensky said. "The deficit of these missiles - that is people's lives." He also confirmed that the US satellite communications system, Starlink – and its military version, Starshield – were still being restricted in occupied areas of Ukraine. Ukrainian drone units have described their problems to the BBC, as their interceptor drones can no longer catch up with Russian Shaheds. It means those weapons then fly deeper into Ukraine, unhindered. So whose decision was that? "Technically SpaceX, politically - I don't know, I really don't know," Zelensky replied. "It's like... ping pong. We are asking one side, they say it's the other." Tough winter Ukraine's own long-range strikes against Russian targets have increased in recent weeks, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel. On Thursday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said an attack that sank a Russian warship docked in eastern Libya this week risked spreading war to the Mediterranean, which was unacceptable. Zelensky defended the move, calling the warship Merkury an "absolutely fair goal". He accepted that such strikes were "very dangerous" but said Ukraine's forces "never attack" without co-ordinating with its partners. He declined to be more specific. But he acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter. Recent attacks on Kyiv have targeted bridges over the vast river Dnipro, apparently trying to cut the city in two. Some residents have already left town for the winter and businesses closed, as power cuts and strikes on logistics networks have pushed operating costs unmanageably high. They have also plunged much of the city into darkness. "[Russia] wants us to run away, of course," Zelensky said. "People can go, but we will try to defend our capital in any way. We need our capital. Without a capital, you don't have a country." articles.title: 42 state attorneys want to stop Character.ai from auctioning private chat histories
articles.summary: Character.AI is planning to sell millions of chat histories, says a group of state attorneys. Illustration by Algi Febri Sugita/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images State attorneys general move to block Character.AI from auctioning millions of private user chats. The objection says that datasets includes account details and sensitive chat histories. They said bankruptcy should not allow Character to sidestep federal and state privacy protections. A group of state attorneys general is asking a bankruptcy court to stop Character.AI from auctioning off millions of users’ private chatbot conversations, including records tied to children, to the highest bidder. In a filing on Tuesday, 42 state attorneys general said that the now- bankrupt AI chatbot company is planning to sell chat histories from 21 million US accounts, more than 2 million of which include children . the December 1 auction would also sell private information such as account details, IP addresses, and other metadata, as well as internal risk scores the company assigned users. The states argue that the terms of sale give users virtually no protection. A buyer would not be required to follow Character.AI’s privacy policy, honor deletion requests, or limit how it uses or resells the data, they said. The attorneys added that Character.AI had previously told users that it did not sell personal information for money. “Character.AI’s plan to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chat histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling,” Bonta said in a statement. According to the states, the datasets include conversations involving self-harm, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts, sexual material and users who treated characters presenting themselves as therapists or doctors. The coalition asked the court to reject the terms of the sale, and the company’s proposed lead bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, an entity formed in Delaware a day before Character.AI selected it for the role. The states say bankruptcy should not allow Character.AI to sidestep federal and state privacy protections, particularly for children. At minimum, they said, any sale should exclude minors’ chats and other sensitive data and impose meaningful conditions on whoever acquires the company’s assets. Character.AI did not respond to a request for comment. Character.AI’s safety practices have faced intense scrutiny and multiple lawsuits. The company, its founders, and Google were sued by the mother of a Florida teenager who alleged that a chatbot fostered an emotionally dependent and sexually exploitative relationship with her 14-year-old son, reinforced his suicidal thoughts, and contributed to his death. Character.AI and Google later reached settlements in teen-harm lawsuits. The startup was founded by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas. In 2024, Google struck a roughly $2.7 billion deal for a nonexclusive license to Character.AI’s technology and brought the founders back to the company, while Character.AI continued operating independently. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October. If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo. articles.title: Iran denies responsibility after two Italians are killed in Kuwait drone strike
articles.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, seen here in September, told the Senate in Rome on Thursday that two Italians were killed in an Iranian drone strike targeting a Kuwaiti military installation. File Photo by Stephani Spindel/UPI Nov. 26 (UPI) -- Two Italians were killed Thursday in a drone strike in Kuwait, officials from both countries confirmed, blaming Iran for the attack. The two unidentified Italian technicians with Rheinmetall Italia were killed at in a drone strike at about 2 p.m. local time on a Kuwaiti military installation, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Italian Senate in Rome. He said the two Italians were working at an air-defense detection station when it was attacked. A Pakistani citizen and a Kuwaiti army captain were also injured, he said. "A powerful explosion occurred and, unfortunately, according to information reaching us from Kuwait, both of our compatriots have died," he said. "On behalf of the government -- and I believe I can speak on behalf of everyone -- I wish to express my solidarity with the families of the Italian victims." The Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the two technicians were performing maintenance on detection antennas for Skyguard air defense system, which is used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces. Kuwaiti Foreign Affairs Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah called Tajani to express his country's solidarity with and support for Italy following the attack, according to a readout of the call . Before the Senate, Tajani stated they were killed by drones of Iranian origin, though Tehran denies responsibility. Iran's Embassy in Rome said it "categorically rejects the allegation," while suggesting the incident could be a so-called false-flag attack conducted to drag Europe into the U.S.-Israel war against Iran. "The Embassy urges all parties to remain vigilant in this regard," it said in a statement . Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi in a social media statement said he expressed his condolences over the deaths of the two Italians in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts. "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war," he said. The deaths come amid escalating hostilities between the United States and Iran, which last week resumed attacks on Kuwait following two months of relative clam in Kuwait. Iran has repeatedly targeted Gulf nations hosting U.S. military assets since the war began with joint U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. articles.title: “笑死，谷歌亲自教你怎么蒸馏 Gemini”
articles.summary: 当某些顶级模型厂商严防死守、生怕被蒸馏时，谷歌直接给了一份企业蒸馏操作指南。 从数据集准备、教师模型配置，到学生模型训练、任务监控和结果评估，谷歌几乎把整个操作流程都写进了文档，甚至连 API 请求示例和训练参数都准备好了。 不过，上面网站目前英文版网页打开后显示 404，其他语言的则都正常显示，不确定该服务目前具体什么情况。 在文档里，谷歌给出的理由也相当“务实”：前沿模型虽然能力强，但对于某些特定企业应用来说，可能配置过高。企业真正需要的，未必是每一次请求都调用最强模型，而是在保证任务质量的前提下，把延迟和成本降下来。 而除了面向企业，谷歌还提供开放模型的监督微调和蒸馏微调服务，该页面显示正常，谷歌列出的蒸馏教师模型包括智谱的 GLM-5.2 MaaS，而学生模型则包括 Qwen 3 和 Gemma 3 系列。 1 训练集不必人工标注，谷歌连蒸馏流程都安排好了 我们先看谷歌这套服务究竟怎么“蒸馏”自己的。 按照官方文档，优享先机（Early Access）阶段支持的组合是：以 Gemini 3.1 Pro 作为教师模型，以 Gemini 2.5 Flash 作为学生模型（注：该模型已退役）。 这里有一个值得注意的区别。 传统监督式微调（SFT）通常需要准备输入和对应的标准答案，模型通过学习这些标注数据来调整自身行为；推理路径蒸馏是“过程监督”的变体，强迫参数量较小的学生模型去模仿旗舰模型的任务拆解、假设验证与逻辑回溯路径。 谷歌蒸馏服务就允许用户直接提供提示词数据集，不必事先准备完整的标准答案，教师模型会根据这些输入生成目标回答，再将结果用于学生模型训练。利用教师模型生成的内部推理路径，也就是文档所称的“原始想法”。这是“推理时代”后，蒸馏技术最关键的分水岭。 对于需要多步逻辑推理、技术文档摘要、复杂编码等任务的企业来说，这种方式尤其值得关注。比如，企业已经发现 Gemini Pro 能够很好地完成某项复杂任务，但直接使用 Pro 模型的调用成本和响应延迟又难以满足业务要求，就可以尝试将其能力迁移到 Flash 级别的学生模型上。 谷歌还把整个流程拆解得非常细致。 首先，企业需要准备自己的提示词数据集，并将其保存为 JSONL 格式，上传到谷歌 Cloud Storage。数据集可以包含系统指令和用户输入，也支持一定形式的多轮对话。 由于后续由教师模型生成目标输出，在训练集准备阶段，企业只需要提供 Prompt，不必提前为每条输入人工标注标准答案。教师模型会自动生成目标回答及相应的原始思考过程，再将其用于学生模型训练。训练完成后，企业仍需要使用独立的留出测试集评估模型表现。 不过，谷歌也给出了明确的数据要求：建议至少准备 1000 个样本，并尽量覆盖实际生产流量中可能出现的不同情况，包括边缘场景和不同长度的提示词。整个训练集最多支持 50000 个样本，JSONL 文件不能超过 1GB。 接下来是教师模型生成阶段。用户需要配置教师模型的生成行为，其中一个重要参数是 candidateCount，即针对每条输入生成多少个回答变体。默认值为 4，允许设置在 1 至 5 之间。 教师模型生成的数据质量，直接影响最终学生模型的表现。谷歌在文档中也特别强调了这一点。 完成数据准备后，就进入学生模型训练阶段。用户需要设置两个主要参数：epochCount 和 learningRateMultiplier。前者决定学生模型需要重复学习整个数据集多少轮，范围为 1 至 100，默认值为 4；后者用于调整学习率，范围为 0.25 至 4，默认值为 1。 整个任务提交后，系统会自动执行教师模型推理和学生模型调优。根据谷歌提供的流程，最终不仅会生成一个注册到模型仓库的蒸馏模型，训练完成后，学生模型会自动注册到 Google Cloud 的 Model Registry，并生成用于推理的专用端点。训练过程中还会保存中间检查点，并为相应检查点提供预测端点，方便开发者比较不同训练阶段的模型表现。 可以看出，企业不需要从零搭建一整套教师模型生成、数据处理、学生模型训练和模型部署流程，谷歌自己把这些环节整合进了云平台服务。 训练完成后，用户还需要使用留出测试集进行评估，并分别与原始 Gemini 2.5 Flash 和 Gemini 3.1 Pro 对比，观察学生模型相较基础模型提升了多少，以及它与教师模型的表现还有多大差距。 从应用场景来看，谷歌给出的方向主要有三类。 第一类是高并发、对延迟敏感的业务。例如，企业需要模型具备 Pro 级别的推理能力，但实际应用又受到严格的延迟服务等级协议（SLA）和预算限制，这时就可以尝试把任务迁移到 Flash 级别模型。 第二类是缺少标准答案的场景。企业可能积累了大量用户查询和业务提示词，却没有足够资源为这些数据逐一标注答案。通过教师模型自动生成训练目标，可以降低数据准备的工作量。 第三类是复杂推理任务，包括多步逻辑、技术文档摘要和复杂编码。基础版 Flash 模型可能难以胜任，但 Pro 模型能够完成，企业就可以尝试通过蒸馏缩小两者之间的能力差距。 这份看起来相当完整的操作手册，也有不少限制。 首先，谷歌明确提醒，使用该服务蒸馏出来的模型只能用于实验和开发，不能部署到生产环境；其次，它还没有向所有用户开放。企业需要联系谷歌，将自己的谷歌云项目加入许可名单，同时启用 Agent Platform API，并获得相应的管理员权限。页面显示，蒸馏任务必须在美国中部的 us-central1 区域运行。首次访问期限为 30 天，默认并发配额为 4。 数据方面也有明显限制：目前只支持文本数据，不支持图片、视频等多模态输入，也不支持函数调用。每条输入最多允许 8000 个 token，如果超过这一限制的样本占比达到 10% 以上，蒸馏任务就会终止。教师模型生成的输出最多为 24000 个 token，超过部分会被截断。 谷歌云官方 Release Notes 显示，Gemini Distillation Service 的 Early Access 于 2026 年 5 月 8 日列入发布记录。也就是说，它并不是最近几天突然推出的服务，但把蒸馏做成生意是谷歌早就想做也在做的事情。 2 不怕蒸馏更便宜，谷歌不只靠模型赚钱 在被打成“反派”之前，蒸馏本来只是一个正常的技术。谷歌很早就发布技术文档对其进行了详细介绍。 而谷歌相对开放的态度，更在于“纯模型厂商”与“全栈云巨头”是完全不同的商业账本。 对于 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 这类以模型能力和 API 服务为核心竞争力的厂商而言，其本质也可以说“Token 批发商”。未经授权的蒸馏会为其带来直接的商业风险：旗舰模型被蒸馏成开源小模型拿去本地或第三方云上部署，这种替代效应可能侵蚀前沿模型厂商的推理收入，也会削弱其在部分应用场景中的定价优势。 但谷歌拥有完整的“芯片（TPU）+ 云计算（GCP）+ 基础模型”全栈生态。谷歌想卖的从来不只是单一模型的 Token，而是围绕 AI 运行的整套云基础设施，这其中当然也包括蒸馏技术带来的便利和优势。 早在 2023 年，谷歌就通过蒸馏将大模型塞进安卓和 iOS 手机本地，支撑起 Gmail 的“帮我撰写”功能；2024 年 9 月，谷歌云 CEO Thomas Kurian 更是明确将“蒸馏、微调与模型适配”列为谷歌云 AI 变现的核心抓手，并披露三星就利用了谷歌的蒸馏工具 Vertex AI 定制 Gemini 与 Imagen 模型，在 Galaxy S24 系列上实现端侧 AI 体验。 这说明，蒸馏对谷歌而言早不只是实验室里的模型优化技术，而是可以直接服务于企业客户、形成商业收入的产品能力。 Thomas 把谷歌云的 AI 变现方式归纳为五种：按照 GPU、TPU 和模型 Token 的使用量收费；通过 Agentspace、Workspace 等产品收取订阅费用；借助 AI 提高客户对其他产品的使用量；根据实际业务价值收费；以及随着客户需求增长，将其升级到功能更强、配额更高的产品版本。 谷歌并不需要让所有企业客户都持续调用最昂贵的模型。对于高并发、对延迟敏感的业务，通过蒸馏，企业有机会降低单次推理成本，同时获得更快的响应速度。 虽然客户可能减少了对高价模型的直接调用，却可以继续使用谷歌云的蒸馏、训练、模型管理和部署服务。原本集中在模型推理环节的支出，也就有机会转化为更广泛的云平台服务需求。谷歌在今年推出的 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform，进一步体现了这种思路。 谷歌的开放模型策略并不局限于自家模型。在面向开放模型的微调与蒸馏服务页面中，已经将智谱 GLM-5.2 MaaS 列为蒸馏教师模型，同时支持使用 Qwen 3 和 Gemma 3 系列作为学生模型。 这种跨厂商的模型组合，体现了谷歌希望将模型训练和适配能力建立在云平台之上，而不是将服务限制在 Gemini 自身生态内。 另外蒸馏完成后，企业也不必将最终模型永久绑定在谷歌云上。完成训练后，开发者可以选择将模型部署到 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 的推理端点，也可以从 Cloud Storage 导出模型权重，部署到其他环境。 3 该防的，还得防 把蒸馏做成赚钱的云服务，绝不意味着谷歌对未经授权的蒸馏行为网开一面。相反，正是因为要保护这门生意的定价权，谷歌的防御手段很是凌厉。 根据谷歌 Threat Intelligence Group（GTIG）今年 9 月发布的报告，攻击者已经开始利用代理基础设施、自动化工具和数千个被盗或欺诈账户，批量收集模型输出。部分协同蒸馏活动涉及超过 1 亿条提示词，目标涵盖文本推理、视觉理解、音频理解以及图像和视频生成。 面对这种“蚂蚁搬家式”的窃取，谷歌已经建立跨账户检测机制，不再只根据单个账户的调用频率判断风险，而是结合实时监测、离线分类器和智能体，识别分散在不同账户和产品渠道中的协同调用。一旦发现异常，还可以采取账户级、项目级限制措施，阻断后续模型访问。 谷歌还开始直接干预蒸馏过程。它已经部署实时主动防御，试图降低未经授权的学生模型从 Gemini 输出中获得的训练收益。谷歌明确表示，这些措施旨在降低蒸馏活动的有效性，甚至削弱学生模型的最终表现。 与此同时，谷歌还在加强对内部推理信息的保护。11 月发布的 Gemini 4 Carbon 安全报告披露，其防御范围已经延伸到思维签名及相关推理轨迹，分别针对跨模型提取和同模型提取进行防护，避免攻击者通过诱导模型输出内部推理信息来复现其能力。 此外，谷歌还表示已经开发出识别 Gemini 蒸馏模型的技术，可以追踪模型来源，并对相关模型采取措施。不过，官方没有公开具体实现方式。 本文来源： 极客邦科技InfoQ 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄金强势反弹，大规模空头挤压一触即发？
articles.summary: 黄金市场正在经历一场剧烈的技术性反转。在经历了数周惨烈抛售、空头头寸大幅积累之后，金价强势拉升，市场正在评估这场反弹能否演变为一轮系统性的空头挤压行情。 金价本周大幅走高，确认了此前图表上出现的"锤形反转"形态。据The Market Ear分析， 金价在触及3400美元关键支撑位后强势反弹，当前面临的首个阻力位在3800美元附近（21日均线），若能有效收于该水平之上，则通往4000美元区域的技术阻力相当有限。 值得注意的是，200日均线目前仍远高于现货价格，均值回归交易空间依然充裕。 此轮反弹的潜在推动力不容小觑。高盛数据显示， 投机者在11月10日至17日期间净卖出93亿美元黄金期货，随后一周抛售进一步加速，黄金在11月17日至20日间暴跌9%，期货未平仓合约总量再减少73亿美元。大规模空头头寸的积累，意味着一旦反弹持续，被迫回补的买盘可能形成强大的正反馈效应。 技术面确认反转，关键阻力位清晰 金价本周的走势在技术层面具有重要意义。The Market Ear指出 ，黄金在3400美元大关触底后形成的锤形K线，与今年3月低点时的形态高度相似——彼时同样出现了锤形反转，随后金价展开了一轮显著上涨。 从周线RSI来看，黄金的动量指标刚刚从9月以来最超卖的水平回升，在动量恢复至中性区域之前，此轮反弹仍有相当大的延伸空间。 不过，从更宏观的视角来看，金价自历史高点以来的下行通道结构依然完整。通道中轨阻力位于3850美元附近，上轨则在4000美元以上。分析人士指出，即便不发生趋势逆转，在下行通道内部的空头挤压行情同样具备可观的交易价值。 黄金抛售规模触目惊心，恐慌情绪量化可见 此轮黄金抛售的规模和速度均属罕见。高盛数据显示，11月10日至17日当周，投机者卖出93亿美元黄金期货，不仅完全逆转了前一周的买入，其中53亿美元来自多头平仓，35亿美元为新增空头建仓。 市场恐慌情绪在期权市场同样得到充分体现。据高盛统计， 黄金3个月隐含波动率与25-delta看跌/看涨期权偏斜度均在上周五录得4至5个标准差的异常波动，偏斜度飙升至多年高位。高盛历史数据显示，自2022年底以来，类似的偏斜度急升在随后一周内约有70%的概率出现回落。 波动率的急剧攀升也给期权买方带来了多重压力。The Market Ear分析指出，随着金价强势反弹，此前高价买入看跌期权的投资者正同时承受方向、波动率和时间价值三重损失。一旦波动率出现实质性回落，相关的Delta对冲操作可能进一步推动买盘涌现，为挤压行情再添燃料。 CTA大规模持空，强制回补或成关键催化剂 系统性交易者的仓位结构，是此轮潜在空头挤压最值得关注的变量之一。 高盛数据显示， 商品交易顾问（CTA）目前持有大量黄金空头头寸，若金价进一步走高，这一群体可能面临被迫大规模回补的压力。 The Market Ear指出， 当前黄金上行的"凸性"正变得愈发引人关注——价格的进一步上涨可能触发CTA的止损回补机制，形成自我强化的买盘循环，从而将一次普通的技术性反弹演变为更具破坏力的空头挤压。 中国资产联动效应值得密切跟踪 黄金与中国创业板指数（ChiNext）之间的高度联动关系，为此轮行情增添了另一个观察维度。 The Market Ear数据显示，两者近期走势保持着异常紧密的相关性，而中国股市最新一轮的挤压行情力度尤为强劲。 分析人士建议密切跟踪这一跨市场关联。若中国权益资产的反弹势头持续，可能为黄金提供额外的上行支撑，进一步强化空头挤压的逻辑链条。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 报道：美国曾敦促委内瑞拉和伊拉克退出OPEC
articles.summary: OPEC内部协调面临新的考验，成员国之间的利益分歧与外部市场竞争，正给这一产油国联盟的稳定性带来更多不确定性。 11月27日，据路透社报道， 特朗普政府曾鼓励委内瑞拉和伊拉克考虑退出OPEC，并阻止委内瑞拉缴纳年度会费。 这一此前未被披露的举动，涉及OPEC五个创始成员国中的两个。 据报道援引十名知情人士，美方官员当时正推动两国扩大石油产量和投资，部分人士担心OPEC的产量限制可能制约这一目标。 相关讨论一度引起沙特方面关注。沙特王储Mohammed bin Salman今夏出面沟通，促使特朗普政府不再推进此事。在伊拉克，总理Ali Faleh al-Zaidi也曾提出退出OPEC的可能性，但最终选择留在组织内。 叠加阿联酋今年宣布退出，OPEC成员国之间的协调问题受到更多关注。 Alpine Macro首席地缘政治策略师Dan Alamariu表示：“OPEC破裂的风险正在上升。” 美国希望扩大石油产量 美国对委内瑞拉和伊拉克的相关讨论，主要围绕两国未来的石油生产和投资展开。 今年1月，美国开始参与管理委内瑞拉国家资金的使用。伊拉克的石油收入则继续通过纽约联邦储备银行的账户流转。 据报道，美国国务院一名官员表示，较低级别官员今年早些时候可能向委内瑞拉方面提出过退出OPEC的问题，但这并非高层官员讨论的议题。对于伊拉克，国务院称，双方对话主要聚焦能源基础设施建设，以及提高石油产量和运输能力。 据报道援引五名知情人士，美国希望吸引石油巨头加大对委内瑞拉的投资，恢复该国石油生产，同时担心OPEC的产量政策可能限制增产空间。沙特王储Mohammed bin Salman随后介入沟通，特朗普政府最终不再推进这一想法。今年8月，特朗普表示，委内瑞拉是否退出OPEC应由该国自行决定。 在伊拉克，美国官员今夏也曾与总理Ali Faleh al-Zaidi讨论退出OPEC的可能性。当时，埃克森美孚和雪佛龙正计划在当地进行重大新投资。 Al-Zaidi随后在政府会议上提出这一问题，但伊拉克石油部倾向于留在组织内，并争取提高产量配额。据报道援引知情人士， 伊拉克国内仍有部分人士支持退出OPEC和OPEC+，认为现有产量安排限制了该国的生产空间，因此这一议题未来仍可能再次出现。 成员流失与产量协调压力 委内瑞拉目前暂时不受OPEC+产量配额限制。多年制裁和管理不善已导致该国石油产量从历史高位大幅下滑。据OPEC数据，委内瑞拉9月日产量约为120万桶。该国国家石油公司PDVSA计划在明年年底前将产量提高至150万桶/日。 OPEC上一次对委内瑞拉实施产量配额是在2017至2018年，当时目标约为200万桶/日。据报道援引一名了解委内瑞拉在OPEC立场的人士表示， 在该国产量恢复至这一水平之前，重新纳入配额体系的可能性不大。 近年来，OPEC成员数量持续减少。阿联酋今年宣布退出，此前安哥拉、厄瓜多尔和卡塔尔已分别于2024年、2020年和2019年退出。 随着成员国对产量配额的诉求出现分化，以及美国石油产量持续增长，OPEC如何协调成员国利益、维持产量政策的一致性，正成为影响其市场地位的重要因素。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “做好准备”！英国人疯狂囤现金：五周额外提取7亿英镑，创2009年金融危机以来次高
articles.summary: 英国民众正以十余年来最快的速度囤积现金，折射出政府应急备灾宣传对公众行为的深远影响。 英国央行数据显示， 截至11月25日的五周内，流通中的现金增加了15亿英镑，其中约7亿英镑（约合9.18亿美元）超出正常水平。这一规模相当于英国一半成年人口每人额外提取25英镑。同期流通中的现金总量增加1.5%，为2014年以来最大单期涨幅。 此轮囤现金潮的直接导火索， 是英国政府于10月22日前后启动的"做好准备"（Be Ready）公众应急宣传活动。 安全事务大臣Dan Jarvis在活动中敦促民众储备足够三天使用的基本物资，包括瓶装水、食品、手摇收音机以及现金，以应对网络攻击、极端天气或其他紧急情况。官方零售销售数据及零售追踪机构Worldpanel by Numerator的数据均显示，罐头食品、超高温灭菌奶、消毒液和瓶装水等耐储存商品销量同步大增，表明公众正在全面响应政府号召。 现金提取规模创本世纪次高，仅次于2009年金融危机 过去五周的现金提取规模约为此前三年同期的两倍。 自2000年以来，唯一一次现金提取量超过本次的时期，是2009年10月至11月全球金融危机期间。 这一对比凸显了本轮囤现金行为的异常程度——其驱动力并非金融系统动荡，而是政府主动引导下的预防性备灾需求。 英国央行拒绝就现金需求激增的原因作出评论。 不过，行长安德鲁·贝利本月早些时候已公开承认存在异常。贝利11月9日在瑞士国际问题研究所发表演讲时表示：" 我们发行的现金数量仍在增加。这是央行领域最大的悖论之一。" 他的表态发生在大规模现金提取已经启动之后，暗示央行内部对这一趋势已有所察觉，但尚未给出明确解释。 备灾行为蔓延至实物商品，消费结构出现短期扭曲 现金囤积只是更广泛备灾行为的组成部分。上周公布的官方零售销售数据显示，罐头食品和超高温灭菌奶等耐储存商品销量明显上升。 零售追踪机构Worldpanel by Numerator的数据进一步显示，英国消费者正在集中采购消毒液、瓶装水和罐头食品。这些数据共同表明，政府的应急宣传活动已对短期消费结构产生实质性影响，部分品类需求出现集中释放。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美团单季赚21亿元，增长向零售和海外延伸
articles.summary: 美团的利润开始修复了。 11月27日，美团发布三季报，营收1156亿元，同比增长21.6%；净利润20.7亿元，上年同期为亏损186.3亿元。核心本地商业经营利润恢复至57亿元，成为此次盈利改善的主要支撑。 这份财报呈现出两个变化，国内主业重新贡献利润，食杂零售和海外业务继续扩张。美团需要解决的问题，也从承受补贴战的亏损，转向如何分配恢复的盈利能力。 利润修复首先来自营销投入的变化。三季度，美团销售及营销开支同比下降20.1%至270亿元，占收入的比例由35.6%降至23.4%。公司将核心本地商业扭亏主要归因于审慎的营销支出，以及收入增长带来的经营杠杆效应。 补贴能够迅速拉高订单量，却也会吸引大量围绕优惠券流动的需求。平台减少这类投入后，订单是否留下、消费者是否愿意按正常价格购买，比促销期间的单量峰值更能体现业务质量。 美团称，三季度外卖行业平均客单价同比明显回升，暑期旺季也带动了经营表现。随着低价竞争趋于理性，平台有机会从争夺每一笔订单，转向改善每笔订单的收益。 不过，盈利恢复还没有进入快速扩张阶段。核心本地商业经营利润与二季度基本持平，经营利润率从7.9%回落至7.3%。暑期骑手补贴增加、季节性营销活动等，仍在影响利润释放。 这意味着，减少补贴带来的改善之后，美团还需要依靠订单密度、配送效率和商户经营能力继续提高回报。配送网络建成后，同一区域内更多稳定订单，有助于分摊运营成本；用户偶尔为了优惠下单，则很难提供同样的价值。 竞争也在向更多商品品类延伸。餐饮外卖积累了高频用户和即时配送网络，即时零售则试图让这张网络承接买菜、日用品等需求，扩大消费者在平台上的支出。 美团的投入已经深入线下。三季度，小象超市在营城市达到85个，并在北京、杭州、深圳等地开设了9家线下门店，社区零售业务快乐猴也在加快开店。 从连接商户到直接经营商品，美团需要承担采购、库存和损耗管理。即时零售的竞争因此不只是谁送得快，还包括商品是否齐全、价格是否稳定，以及补货是否及时。 优惠券可以短期改变消费者在哪里下单，供应链效率才能决定平台能否长期提供有竞争力的价格。这类投入见效更慢，却直接影响复购和毛利。 新业务的财务表现已经出现效率改善。三季度，该板块收入373亿元，同比增长32.9%，经营亏损由二季度的17.4亿元收窄至13.1亿元。收入扩张与环比减亏同时发生，为继续投入提供了空间。 海外也是资金的重要去向。据美团披露，Keeta已在中国香港和沙特先后实现盈利，并以圣保罗为中心拓展巴西业务，覆盖32座城市。成熟市场开始贡献经营成果，新市场仍需要建设商户和配送网络。 主业恢复盈利之后，平台正在把竞争延伸到商品供给、线下经营和海外履约。 对美团而言，下一步的关键是让这些投入形成稳定收入，同时守住国内主业刚刚修复的利润。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 奇瑞加码非插电混动，争夺不充电的家庭用户
articles.summary: 奇瑞正在给非插电混动车增加新的竞争筹码。 11月27日，广州车展开幕，全新瑞虎8 PLUS首次亮相。据了解，新车引入约5千瓦时电池的HEV混动方案，搭载猎鹰700驾驶辅助系统及激光雷达，支持城市领航辅助、全场景泊车，并提供五座和七座布局。现场报道显示，其混动版本电池容量为5.1千瓦时。 这款车的变化集中在两个方面，扩大混动电池容量，并将城市驾驶辅助引入非插电车型。奇瑞希望争取的，是仍习惯加油、同时希望获得更多电驱和智能化体验的家庭用户。 非插电混动保留了加油补能的使用方式，适合没有固定充电条件、或不愿安排充电行程的消费者。但这类用户在选车时，同样会比较座舱、驾驶辅助和驻车功能。动力形式不同，并不意味着他们愿意接受明显的配置差距。 瑞虎8 PLUS此次强调更大的电池，正是要拓宽混动系统的用途。 按照奇瑞公布的产品方案，新车将提供哨兵模式、小憩模式等功能，把电池的作用从行驶环节延伸到停车后的用车场景。对家庭SUV而言，这些功能能否方便地使用，比单独强调电池容量更有意义。 不过，电池增加也会带来重量和成本。非插电车型主要依靠发动机和制动能量回收补充电能，更大的电池并不直接等于更低的油耗。奇瑞需要在电量管理、发动机介入与车内用电之间做好匹配，让用户感受到的便利足以覆盖增加的购车成本。 驾驶辅助是另一项变化。按照此次发布的配置，瑞虎8 PLUS将激光雷达、城市领航辅助和泊车功能纳入产品方案。这意味着，奇瑞对这款家庭SUV的竞争力判断，已经超出动力、油耗和空间。 城市领航辅助的加入，有助于缩小非插电车型与智能电动车之间的功能差距。对消费者而言，是否选择混动，可以更多取决于补能条件和出行习惯。但硬件只是起点，实际体验还取决于软件成熟度、功能开放范围及后续更新。 这也让瑞虎8 PLUS面临更直接的价格比较。消费者会把它与同价位燃油车、插混车放在一起，比较购买成本、日常油耗和配置。 对于具备便利充电条件的家庭，插混车型仍有吸引力；非插电混动要争取的是那些重视使用便利、又不想放弃智能化功能的用户。 奇瑞此次车展的产品安排，也体现出多种动力路线并行。 全新艾瑞泽7开启预售，搭载1.5T发动机；瑞虎8 PLUS则以混动与驾驶辅助升级切入家庭SUV市场。两款车共同说明，在推进新能源产品的同时，奇瑞仍在更新以加油为主要补能方式的产品。 对奇瑞而言，这套组合能否成立，最终还要看最终价格。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美团Q3扭亏：利润回来了，但“边界”问题没有
articles.summary: 11月27日，美团发布第三季度财报，其营收1156亿元，同比增长21.6%；经调整净利润18.5亿元，而去年同期是经调整净亏损160.1亿元。在连续多个季度的亏损之后，美团重新回到了盈利轨道上。核心本地商业经营利润57亿元，上年同期为经营亏损141亿元，同比减亏显著；新业务收入373亿元，同比增长32.9%，经营亏损收窄至13亿元。 把这份财报放在更长的时间轴上看，它的意义不在于“扭亏”本身。过去一年多，美团经历了一场代价高昂的外卖补贴战，单季经调整净亏损一度超过160亿元。如今扭亏兑现，标志着那场消耗战的账面伤口开始愈合。然而，利润修复的路径、竞争格局的固化方式，以及AI与国际化在新叙事中的真实位置，共同指向一个更根本的问题：美团用利润换来的，究竟是一段可持续的修复期，还是仅仅是从一场战争转入另一场更漫长的消耗？ 利润是怎么回来的：补贴退坡、提质减量与新业务减亏 拆解利润修复的来源，比利润数字本身更值得关注。 最直接的推动力是补贴退坡。外卖单均补贴从2025年三季度的2.6—2.8元降至2026年9月的1.3—1.4元，带动单均UE（单位经济模型）回到正值区间，9月约0.4元。补贴的收缩不是美团的主动选择，而是竞争环境变化的被动结果：当淘宝闪购和京东外卖在补贴战中也开始承受利润压力，继续加码补贴的边际收益迅速递减，行业从“谁补贴更多”转向“谁先停下来”。 但美团利润修复的质量，在很大程度上取决于“怎么停”。美团没有简单地回到补贴战前的规模扩张逻辑，而是采取了一种“提质减量”的策略：放弃部分低价订单，力保高价值用户和餐饮场景中的份额，用更高的客单价来弥补日均单量的微降。核心本地商业营收增长16.8%，经营利润却从亏损141亿元直接翻正至57亿元，说明利润改善的主要驱动力来自单均经济模型的修复，而非规模扩张。 新业务减亏则提供了第二层支撑。新业务经营亏损率从上年同期的4.6%收窄至3.5%，亏损绝对额控制在13亿元。小象超市在营城市数达到85个，Keeta在香港和沙特先后实现盈利。这些业务不再是无底洞式的投入，开始展现出可收敛的边界。 不过，利润修复的脆弱性同样明显。骑手成本正在成为一项刚性约束。2026年7月起，新就业形态人员职业伤害保障试点扩至全国，美团也取消了超时扣款并推进养老保险补贴。单均履约成本环比上升0.2—0.3元，三季度单均UE大概率低于二季度的0.16元。利润回来了，但每一分利润的“含金量”，都比补贴战之前更薄。 竞争格局：5:4:1之后，“和平”的代价 理解美团这份财报，绕不开它在一个已经固化的竞争格局中的位置。 综合高盛、瑞银、易观等多份测算，2026年三季度美团、淘宝（含饿了么、淘宝闪购）、京东的餐饮外卖市场份额大致稳定在5:4:1。易观口径下，美团份额为52.2%，淘宝43.5%，京东4.3%。不同机构的具体数字存在口径差异，但方向一致：美团守住了五成左右的基本盘，行业从“一超多强”变成了“双强对峙”，补贴大战进入收尾阶段。 格局稳定对美团是好事，但它同时意味着两件事。第一，美团不再拥有绝对定价权。在5:4:1的结构下，任何一方单方面提高变现率，都可能触发用户和商家向对手迁移，利润率的上行空间被竞争结构本身所限制。第二，竞争的重心已经从“烧钱抢份额”转向“效率比拼”。三家平台同步减亏、份额却没有明显挪动，说明继续用补贴改变格局的性价比已经极低，接下来的竞争将围绕单位经济模型、供给密度和履约稳定性展开。 这对美团有利的一面在于，它的履约网络密度和餐饮场景的用户心智仍然是行业中最深的护城河之一。第三方测算显示，美团外卖单均履约成本约6.5元，竞品约6.9元，0.3—0.5元的差距主要来自订单密度。但这种优势是“防守型”的：它能帮助美团在效率竞争中不被侵蚀，却不足以支撑过去那种“无边界扩张”的估值叙事。 更值得警惕的信号来自到店业务。外卖是流量入口，到店酒旅才是利润的核心来源。抖音本地生活2025年支付GMV超过8500亿元，在流量降维打击下，美团到店业务的经营利润率已从巅峰期的45%左右回落至26.5%附近。外卖利润修复的另一个含义，是美团需要用这笔利润同时应对到店业务的利润率承压、骑手福利的刚性成本，以及AI和新业务的持续投入。扭亏不是终点，而是资源约束下新一轮取舍的起点。 AI与国际化：增量叙事的现实边界 当核心业务的利润天花板变得可见，市场自然会把目光投向新叙事。美团在AI和国际化上都有动作，但两者的战略含义截然不同。 AI方面，三季度研发投入77亿元，同比增长11.3%；AI经营工作台“妙手”已服务超过200万商家；11月，美团发布并开源了LongCat-2.5大模型。王兴在早前的沟通中明确表态：美团“不会成为Token工厂”，AI产品用于支持核心业务，从信息查询逐步发展为执行任务，并推动内部工作流程的效率提升。这一姿态是务实的，它把AI定位为加固本地生活交易入口的“铲子”，防止AI Agent绕过美团直接完成交易。但务实也意味着，AI在可预见的未来更可能体现为成本节约和商家粘性，而非独立的收入引擎。 国际化的情况类似，但多了一层可验证性。Keeta在香港用时29个月实现盈利，在沙特仅用22个月，7月已录得盈利，巴西则以圣保罗为重心控制预算、覆盖32座城市。沙特盈利的意义在于，它初步验证了美团履约模型在海外市场的可复制性，而不仅仅是“又一个烧钱故事”。但海外业务的体量尚小，主流估值几乎未将其计入，短期内很难对冲核心业务利润率的结构性压力。 估值的分歧：修复已经发生，重估尚未到来 机构对这份财报的整体态度偏多。花旗维持“买入”评级、目标价120港元；瑞银认为即时零售及到店竞争缓和将支持美团未来多年的盈利复苏。但股价的表现说明了更复杂的故事：财报前，美团股价连跌七日，一度创下七年新低61.05港元，绩前才出现反弹。 这种反差指向一个核心分歧：市场承认利润修复正在发生，但对修复的“斜率”和“持续性”缺乏信心。补贴退坡带来的利润反弹是一次性的还是可延续的？骑手成本上升会不会吞噬UE修复的空间？到店业务的利润率压力会不会迫使美团重新加大投入？AI和海外业务在多久之后才能对利润表产生实质性贡献？这些问题在财报数字中找不到完整答案。 美团的Q3财报证明了一件事：它有足够韧性的基本盘，能够在补贴战最残酷的阶段守住份额，并在战事降温后迅速把利润拉回正值。但它没有证明的是，当“无边界扩张”的叙事被消耗殆尽之后，一个以本地生活为圆心、以效率和AI为半径的“有边界防守”模式，能否支撑起下一个阶段的增长预期。利润回来了，但关于边界的答案，还没有。 本文来自： Tech商业 风险提示及免责条款
